title: Trace Orchestra Conductor Profiling
body:
Objective:
Quick, reproducible exploration of the long-tail E2E latency behavior observed on the v2 serving runtime (public fleet). We want: 1) a compact per-stage decomposition for p50/p95/p99, 2) a small set of high-confidence hypotheses for root causes, and 3) actionable experiments to run in the next sprint.

Context / why now:
Over the last two weeks we've seen intermittent p99 spikes (clients reported 10x slower responses on small chat completions). Dashboard snapshots: overall generation p50=14ms, p95=64ms, p99=320ms. Spike pattern looks correlated with bursty multi-route traffic and a handful of long-seqlen traces. This doc gathers trace excerpts and preliminary attributions.

Methodology (how traces were selected):
- Sampled traces via the SLO-driven sampler (slo-sample window 100s, weight p99-biased).
- Focus set: 200 traces in the 250–600ms wall-clock bucket from the last 48h on region-us-west1, model-family: rw-base-13b (quantized).
- For each trace we stitch stage spans: (http-ingest -> tokenization -> request-queue -> batcher-wait -> kernel-exec(s) -> kv-lookup -> emit -> egress).
- Derived per-stage percentiles using per-trace summed durations.

High-level numbers (sample cohort, region=us-west1, model=rw-base-13b):
- End-to-end: p50=12ms, p95=72ms, p99=330ms
- Median per-stage breakdown (p95 cohort): tokenization 1.2ms (6%), request-queue 8.6ms (12%), batcher-wait 22.4ms (31%), kernel-exec 17.8ms (24%), kv-lookup 9.5ms (13%), emit+egress 3.2ms (4%)

Observation 1 — Batcher wait dominates many p99 traces:
- In ~62% of p99 traces the 'batcher-wait' stage alone accounts for >25% of wall time. We see groups of traces where batcher waits stack: backends receive many small requests that are not coalescing well (arrival jitter).
- Representative trace (timestamps are relative to request start):
  - 0.0ms http-ingest
  - 0.8ms tokenization 0.8ms
  - 2.1ms request-queue 1.3ms
  - 15.2ms batcher-wait 13.1ms
  - 36.0ms kernel-exec 20.8ms
  - 46.9ms kv-lookup 10.9ms
  - 52.1ms emit 5.2ms
  - 54.3ms egress 2.2ms
- Notes: batcher-wait spikes are often accompanied by small jittered arrivals from upstream clients (PLG bursts + multi-route fan-in).

Observation 2 — Kernel execution variance for longer sequences:
- Kernel-exec time scales with seqlen non-linearly; for sequences > 1k tokens p95 kernel-exec jumps significantly. In our p99 bucket some traces are misclassified (seqlen reported low in request metadata but stage snapshot shows extended kernel time) — suggests mismatch between client-declared seqlen and actual token emission pattern (clients using streaming with longer followups).
- Example: two traces with similar declared seqlen=64 but kernel-exec 18ms vs 120ms. The longer one had repeated small emits (backpressure + micro-batching).

Observation 3 — KV-cache misses amplify p99 tail:
- KV lookup stage shows bimodality. In ~25% of p99 traces kv-lookup latency >40ms, typically tied to cache miss + fallback to slower index (remote sharded store).
- When kv-lookup is slow, kernel-exec often waits for KV results due to dependency on cached keys for attention.

Observation 4 — Request-queue congestion during microbursts:
- A few traces show request-queue durations of 30–90ms, usually when regional ingress has brief saturation and requests wait behind a single noisy tenant with large footprint.

Correlation notes:
- Batcher-wait correlates with high small-request QPS spikes from PLG onboarding flows and with clients that set max_tokens low and do many short completions.
- KV misses correlate with particular model-variant builds deployed last week (build 2025.09.29; PR linked). We should test rollback.

Hypotheses (ranked by confidence):
1) Arrival jitter and small-RPS fan-in cause batcher not to coalesce efficiently -> longer batcher-wait -> p99 tail. (High confidence)
2) A regression in quantized kernel scheduling (PR #7890) increases kernel exec variance on some sequences -> p99 outliers. (Medium confidence)
3) KV cache sharding occasionally routes to a cold shard under sustained churn causing expensive misses -> adds 40–120ms to trace. (Medium confidence)
4) Egress slowdowns (network egress throttling) are rare and explain a tiny fraction of p99. (Low confidence)

Immediate experiments (next 7 days):
- Experiment A: Enable arrival-smoothing heuristic at the batcher (soft 4ms delay for small queuing class) on a canary subset (10% hostpool). Measure p95/p99 and overall latency impact. Owner: Riley. Linear: CONDUCT-212.
- Experiment B: Rollback kernel scheduling PR (7890) in a dedicated staging fleet and replay the long-seqlen traces. Owner: Marcus. GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/7890
- Experiment C: Add shard-hotness telemetry for KV store (emit per-shard miss-rate and 99-latency). Quick instrument and ship a 24h sample. Owner: Sofia. Jira: JIRA-RT-1023.

Instrumentation / data collection improvements:
- Capture per-batch composition metadata in traces (batch size, per-batch request ids) — currently unavailable in ~40% of traces which limits attribution.
- Add a small histogram for 'batcher-idle-wait' with microsecond buckets, export to traces.
- Surface a combined timeline view that overlays ingress QPS, per-host queue depth, and batcher wait; this will make microburst cause-and-effect explicit in dashboards.

Low-effort mitigations (if experiments delayed):
- Rate-limit noisy-tenant at ingress when per-tenant queue depth spikes. Quick mitigation with DDoS-like backpressure policy.
- Temporarily increase coalesce timeout for small requests on high-latency days (config flag).

Acceptance criteria for success:
- Experiment A: reduce batcher-wait contribution to p99 traces by >=30% and overall p99 end-to-end by >=20% for the canary pool without increasing p50 by more than 5%.
- Experiment B: reproduce kernel variance; if rollback reduces kernel-exec p99 by >=40%, prioritize revert.

Follow-ups / action items:
- [Riley] Kick off canary for arrival-smoothing (due 2025-10-07).
- [Marcus] Stage rollback tests and trace replay (due 2025-10-06).
- [Sofia] Ship shard hotness telemetry and 24h sample (due 2025-10-09).
- [Aisha] Prepare short triage write-up for oncall and schedule sync with SRE and serving runtime tomorrow.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there client SDK patterns causing repeated tiny completions? (Need SDK team to sample representative client traffic.)
- Is the quantized kernel variance limited to specific hardware (A100 vs H100) or system config? (Need cross-hardware trace comparison.)

Notes to self:
- Keep sample traces and provenance raw; do not redact in working doc. Some user-facing incidents were tied to the same trace signatures.
- If experiments show arrival-smoothing shifts latency to p50 for some paths, consider adaptive dynamic coalescing rather than fixed timeout.

Appendix — short trace snippet (raw span dump):
SPAN: req=abc123 | host=usw1-host-22 | model=rw-base-13b-q
  span.http-ingest start=0.000 end=0.900 dur=0.900
  span.tokenize start=0.900 end=1.600 dur=0.700
  span.req-queue start=1.600 end=3.800 dur=2.200
  span.batcher-wait start=3.800 end=26.200 dur=22.400
  span.kernel-exec start=26.200 end=45.950 dur=19.750
  span.kv-lookup start=45.950 end=56.100 dur=10.150
  span.emit start=56.100 end=59.500 dur=3.400
  span.egress start=59.500 end=60.300 dur=0.800

If helpful I can: 1) attach the raw trace bundle (200 traces) to CONDUCT-212, 2) run a targeted smoke on the canary pool, or 3) produce a short slide deck for oncall review.

-- Aisha (notes, draft)
